info.title: Fiber AI API
info.description:
# Welcome to the Fiber AI API!



Get your API key at <https://fiber.ai/app/api>.

## Authentication

Include your API key in **one** of the following ways (listed in priority order):

**Option 1 — Request body (POST) or query params (GET):**
```json
{
"apiKey": "YOUR_API_KEY"
}
```

For a GET request, you can include your API key in the query params like this:
```
?apiKey=YOUR_API_KEY
```

**Option 2 — `x-api-key` header:**
```
x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY
```

**Option 3 — `Authorization` header (Bearer token):**
```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
```

If an API key is provided in both the body/query and a header, the body/query value takes precedence.

## Rate limits

Each endpoint has its own rate limit, and if you exceed it you will get a '429' error. Please contact us if you'd like to request a higher rate limit.

## Client timeouts

Some sync endpoints perform live data fetches or multi-step enrichment and can take longer than the default HTTP client timeout (often 30s). Endpoints that require extra time display a **Recommended timeout** badge in their documentation. Configure your HTTP client's timeout to at least the recommended value before calling those endpoints to avoid premature connection drops.

## Troubleshooting

Need help? Write to adi@fiber.ai or your contact on the Fiber team.

## Webhooks

Fiber can send webhook notifications to your application when certain events occur. You can configure your webhook endpoints at <https://fiber.ai/app/api> (the same page where you manage your API keys).

For a full list of available webhook event types, see <https://www.svix.com/event-types/us/org_36NygGf4vTv8iDHHZgXdCNazcJx/>.

# SDKs & MCP

Integrate the Fiber API into your applications with official SDKs or via **MCP** (Model Context Protocol) for LLM and AI agents.

- **[llms.txt](/llms.txt)** — Agent-facing index (routing, MCP workflows, links to `/ai-docs/`).
- **Node.js SDK:** <https://www.npmjs.com/package/@fiberai/sdk>
- **Python SDK:** <https://pypi.org/project/fiberai/>
- **[Fiber SDKs](https://docs.fiber.ai/article/fiber-sdks)** — Client libraries and usage guides for your language or framework.
- **[Using MCP in LLMs](https://docs.fiber.ai/article/using-mcp-in-llms)** — Connect Claude, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible tools to Fiber.
- **[Developing with AI agents](https://docs.fiber.ai/article/developing-with-ai-agents)** — Plugins, MCP servers, skills, and quickstart for building with Fiber in your IDE.

---

post.description: Polls a batch contact details task. Returns partial results as they complete. Call this endpoint repeatedly until the 'done' field is true. Use the task ID returned from the 'Start batch contact details' endpoint. ⚡ Rate limit: 240 requests per 1 minute

taskId.description: The task ID from the start endpoint response.

cursor.description: The pagination cursor from the previous poll response. Omit for the first request.

take.description: The number of people to return per page. Defaults to 100.

totalPeopleToFetch.description: The total number of people in this batch task.

numCompleted.description: The number of people for which contact reveal has completed successfully.

numFailed.description: The number of people for which enrichment failed (no data found or error occurred).

numRemaining.description: The number of people currently being processed (in progress).

numRejected.description: The number of people rejected before queueing because healing failed (for example, an invalid or unresolvable LinkedIn URL).

numDuplicates.description: The number of duplicates found in the input.

overallStats.description: The overall statistics for the batch enrichment task.

done.description: Whether the batch task has finished. When true, check the 'failed' field to determine if it completed successfully or failed.

failed.description: Whether the batch task failed. If true, the task encountered an error and won't be retried. If false and done=true, the task completed successfully. If done=false, this field indicates current processing state.

value.description: A LinkedIn URL, like 'https://www.linkedin.com/in/jake'

inputs.description: The input details provided for this person.

outputs.description: The reveal result for this person.

pageResults.description: The array of results for each person in the current page.

nextCursor.description: The pagination cursor for the next page of results.

post.description: Generates an organizational depth chart for a company — a close analog to the company's internal org chart. Classifies employees by function (Engineering, Sales, Marketing, etc.) and seniority level (Junior through Executive). This is asynchronous: call this endpoint to start generation, then poll /depth-chart/poll with the returned report ID. Processing typically takes 1-5 minutes depending on company size. Depth chart generation processes up to 10,000 employee profiles per report; larger companies are truncated to the most relevant profiles. ⚡ Rate limit: 30 requests per 1 minute

When omitted, functions are auto-detected based on the company's employee titles. An 'Other' category is automatically appended if not already included, to catch employees that don't fit the provided labels.

post.description: Search LinkedIn posts using keyword-based queries. Returns a paginated list of posts matching the search criteria, up to 50 per page. **Keyword Search Syntax:** - **Exact phrase:** Wrap keywords in quotes for exact phrase matching. "head of sales" matches the exact phrase, not the individual words. - **AND:** Use **AND** between keywords to require both terms. sales **AND** engineering matches posts containing both words. - **OR:** Use **OR** between keywords to match posts containing any of the terms. sales **OR** marketing matches posts with either word. - **NOT:** Use **NOT** before a keyword to exclude posts containing that term. sales **NOT** recruiter matches posts with "sales" but without "recruiter". - **Parentheses:** Group terms to control operator precedence. (sales **OR** marketing) **AND** "series A" finds posts about either sales or marketing that also mention "series A". **Order of precedence:** 1. **Quotes (" "):** Exact phrase match. Phrase matching occurs before any Boolean logic is applied. 2. **Parentheses (()):** Used to explicitly group Boolean logic. Grouped expressions are evaluated before ungrouped logic. 3. **NOT:** Applied after any parentheses or quoted phrases are resolved. 4. **AND:** Evaluated after **NOT** but before **OR**. 5. **OR:** Lowest precedence among Boolean operators. ⚡ Rate limit: 120 requests per 1 minute 💰 Cost: 2 credits per page of results ⓘ

keywords.description: Keywords to search for in LinkedIn posts (comma-separated)

recency.description: Filter by post age. Options: Day, Week, Month, Quarter, HalfYear, Year. Defaults to all time if omitted.

post.description: Search for a person using a variety of parameters such as LinkedIn slug, LinkedIn URL, email, or current company information. Returns profile data for the person if found. Providing more information (e.g. name + company + LinkedIn) improves match accuracy. ⚡ Rate limit: 120 requests per 1 minute 💰 Cost: Pay per person: 2 credits per lookup, plus 2 additional credits when the liveFetch flag is set. ⓘ ⏱ Recommended timeout: 30 seconds ⓘ

value.description: The LinkedIn slug of the person (e.g. 'williamhgates' from linkedin.com/in/williamhgates).
The LinkedIn URL of the person (e.g. 'https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates'). The https:// and www prefixes are optional.
The LinkedIn user ID of the person.

profileIdentifier.description: LinkedIn profile identifier (slug or URL). Provides the best match accuracy.

emailAddress.description: Email address to look up. Second-best accuracy after profileIdentifier.

value.description: The name of the person to search for. It can have first name and/or last name. Try to pass in names as present on LinkedIn.

looseMatch.description: If true, allows partial and out-of-order matches. If false, only exact full name matches are returned.

personName.description: Person's name for matching. Best used with companyDomain or companyIdentifier.

value.description: The job title of the person to search for
The LinkedIn slug of the person's current company.
The LinkedIn URL of the person's current company.
The LinkedIn organization ID of the person's current company.

value.description: The headline of the person's LinkedIn profile. This is the first line of their profile.

looseMatch.description: Whether to allow a loose match on the headline. If true, we allow for additional words between the terms in the headline (e.g. 'Software Engineer' would match 'Software Development Engineer'). If false, we require a strict phrase match.

value.description: The name of the company the person is currently working at
The domain of the company the person is currently working at

companyDomain.description: Domain of the person's current company (e.g. 'fiber.ai'). Used with personName for matching.

stateName.description: State or region name in plain text (e.g. 'California', 'New York').

locality.description: Free-text location string. Use this when the location data does not clearly separate into country, state, or city.

profileLocation.description: Location of the person. Accepts country code, state name, and/or a free-text locality string.

numProfiles.description: Maximum number of profile results to return per lookup. Defaults to 1.

liveFetch.description: When true, triggers a real-time LinkedIn profile fetch. Costs additional credits. Useful for profiles not yet in the database or to get the freshest data.

forceCompanyMatch.description: When true, requires that the matched profile works at the specified company. Without this, the API may return profiles that match by name but work elsewhere.

value.description: The name of the school the person is currently attending or has attended. If provided, we will lookup the person by school name.
The LinkedIn organization ID of the school
The LinkedIn URL of the school

value.description: The domain of the school the person is currently attending or has attended. If provided, we will lookup the person by school domain.

fuzzySearch.description: When true, enables fuzzy name matching. Useful when exact name spelling is uncertain.

getDetailedEducation.description: When true, returns detailed_education[] with school_details for each education entry.

getDetailedWorkExperience.description: When true, returns detailed_work_experiences[] with company_details (domains, preferred_name, linkedin_primary_slug, li_org_id) for each work experience. Use this to get company domains for a person.

post.description: Search for many people using a variety of parameters such as LinkedIn slug, LinkedIn URL, or current company information. Returns profile data for each person if found. value.description: The domain of the company the person is currently working at

companyDomain.description: Domain of the person's current company (e.g. 'fiber.ai'). Used with personName for matching.

value.description: The name of the company the person is currently working at
The job title of the person to search for
The name of the person to search for. It can have first name and/or last name. Try to pass in names as present on LinkedIn.

looseMatch.description: If true, allows partial and out-of-order matches. If false, only exact full name matches are returned.

personName.description: Person's name for matching. Best used with companyDomain or companyIdentifier.

numProfiles.description: Maximum number of profile results to return per lookup. Defaults to 1.

value.description: The LinkedIn slug of the person (e.g. 'williamhgates' from linkedin.com/in/williamhgates).
The LinkedIn URL of the person (e.g. 'https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates'). The https:// and www prefixes are optional.
The LinkedIn user ID of the person.

profileIdentifier.description: LinkedIn profile identifier (slug or URL). Provides the best match accuracy.

value.description: The LinkedIn slug of the person's current company.
The LinkedIn URL of the person's current company.
The LinkedIn organization ID of the person's current company.

companyIdentifier.description: LinkedIn identifier for the person's current company. Used with personName for matching.

emailAddress.description: Email address to look up. Second-best accuracy after profileIdentifier.

items.description: Parameters for searching for a person. Provide at least one parameter. More parameters improve match accuracy.

liveFetch.description: When true, triggers a real-time LinkedIn profile fetch. Costs additional credits. Useful for profiles not yet in the database or to get the freshest data.

forceCompanyMatch.description: When true, requires that the matched profile works at the specified company. Without this, the API may return profiles that match by name but work elsewhere.

fuzzySearch.description: When true, enables fuzzy name matching. Useful when exact name spelling is uncertain.

getDetailedEducation.description: When true, returns detailed_education[] with school_details for each education entry.

getDetailedWorkExperience.description: When true, returns detailed_work_experiences[] with company_details (domains, preferred_name, linkedin_primary_slug, li_org_id) for each work experience. Use this to get company domains for a person.

x-credit-cost.description: Pay per person: 2 credits per lookup, plus 2 additional credits when the liveFetch flag is set.
x-credit-cost.comment: LinkedIn live fetch credits only apply when the liveFetch flag is set.

data.description: Profiles found for each lookup. A 2D array because each lookup may yield multiple profiles.

message.description: Additional context if no matching profile was found.

post.summary: Search companies and prospects from text
post.description:
Takes free-form text (e.g., 'Senior Product Managers from Series A to C FinTech startups in New York') and produces standardized filters (industries, funding stages, headcount ranges, locations, titles, seniorities, etc.). When limits are provided, executes the search and returns matching companies and people in a single synchronous call. When referencing specific companies, provide the identifier in one of these forms: plain name (e.g. 'Apple'), domain (e.g. 'apple.com'), or LinkedIn slug (e.g. 'company/banco-santander').Note: This is not optimized for job descriptions. If you have a JD, use the Search profiles from a job description endpoint instead. ⚡ Rate limit: 120 requests per 1 minute 💰 Cost: Fixed costs per request:
• 2 credits for company search params generation based on prompt, if required
• 2 credits for profile search params generation based on prompt, if required

Additional credits are charged for each company and profile returned, based on the search results. ⓘ ⏱ Recommended timeout: 1 minute ⓘ

query.description: Describe what you’re looking for — for example: I want Senior Product Managers from Series A to C FinTech startups located in New York.

pageSize.description: The number of companies to return per page. Pass null if you only want profiles. NOTE: your companies search params will still get honored to find the profiles.

exclusionListIDs.description: The IDs of company exclusion lists to filter out matching companies.

pageSize.description: The number of profiles to return per page.

exclusionListIDs.description: The IDs of prospect exclusion lists to filter out matching people.

getDetailedEducation.description: Whether to include deep details about each educational item, like the school's LinkedIn URL, website, location, etc. That'll be put in the detailedEducation array. This slows down the API call, so only enable this if you need it.

getDetailedWorkExperience.description: Whether to include deep details about each work experience item, like the company's LinkedIn URL, website, location, etc. That'll be put in the detailedWorkExperience array. This slows down the API call, so only enable this if you need it.

x-credit-cost.description:
Fixed costs per request:
• 2 credits for company search params generation based on prompt, if required
• 2 credits for profile search params generation based on prompt, if required

Additional credits are charged for each company and profile returned, based on the search results.

post.description: AI-powered natural language search across multiple sources (LinkedIn, Google Maps, web, and more). Ideal for local business search where companies/employees have spotty web or LinkedIn presence. **Pagination flow:** 1. **First page** — send `{ search: { request: "initial", query: "...", pageSize: 10 } }`. The `pageSize` you choose here is locked for the entire session. 2. **Subsequent pages** — send `{ search: { request: "subsequent", cursor: "" } }`. 3. When `nextCursor` is `null` in the response, there are no more results. ⚡ Rate limit: 120 requests per 1 minute 💰 Cost: Credits are charged after the search completes based on results: 2 credits per company found and 2 credits per prospect found. Each query resolves to either companies or prospects, so only one rate applies per page. ⓘ

request.description: Use "initial" for the first page of a new search. Provide query, pageSize, and any filters.

query.description: Natural language search query, e.g. "pizza shops in NYC" or "Series A SaaS founders in London". The API infers whether to return companies or people.

pageSize.description: Number of results per page (default 10, max 1000). This value is locked for the entire pagination session.

country_codes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes (e.g. USA, GBR).

min_relevance.description: Minimum relevance score (0.0–1.0). Higher values mean a closer match to your query.

funding_stages.description: Last funding round stage filter. Acquired, public, closed, and unknown stages are not supported.

employee_growth.description: Year-over-year employee growth trend. Elements are OR-ed together.

website_traffic.description: Monthly website traffic bucket filter. Elements are OR-ed together.

employee_count.description: Filter by number of employees (inclusive range).

founded_year.description: Filter by company founding year (inclusive range).

is_b2b.description: If `true`, include only B2B companies. If `false`, exclude B2B companies.

is_tech.description: If `true`, include only tech companies. If `false`, exclude tech companies.

is_saas.description: If `true`, include only SaaS companies. If `false`, exclude SaaS companies.

is_startup.description: If `true`, include only startup-stage companies. If `false`, exclude startups.

website_traffic_growth.description: Year-over-year website traffic growth trend. Elements are OR-ed together.

has_linkedin_page.description: If `true`, include only companies with a LinkedIn page. If `false`, exclude them.

has_employees_on_linkedin.description: If `true`, include only companies that have employees listed on LinkedIn. If `false`, exclude them.

has_public_emails.description: If `true`, include only companies with public contact emails. If `false`, exclude them.

has_company_phone.description: If `true`, include only companies with a phone number. If `false`, exclude them.

hiring_is.description: If `true`, include only companies that are currently hiring. If `false`, exclude them.

is_ai.description: If `true`, include only AI-related companies. If `false`, exclude them.

companyFilters.description: Optional filters applied on top of the AI-derived company filters (e.g. country, funding stage, employee count, etc).

country_codes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes (e.g. USA, GBR).

min_relevance.description: Minimum relevance score (0.0–1.0). Higher values mean a closer job-title match.

include.description: Job titles to search for. Abbreviations are supported (e.g. 'CTO'). Elements are OR-ed together.

exclude.description: Job title keywords to exclude from results.

max_people_per_company.description: Maximum number of people to return per matched company.

company_linkedin_ids.description: Restrict results to people from these companies. Provide the numeric LinkedIn company IDs returned by Fiber's company search endpoints.

peopleFilters.description: Optional filters applied on top of the AI-derived people filters (e.g. job titles, country, max people per company). Only used when the query resolves to a people search.

request.description: Use "subsequent" for page 2 and beyond. Only the cursor from the previous response is required; all other parameters are stored server-side.

cursor.description: The `nextCursor` value returned by the previous response. Valid for 3 days.

x-credit-cost.description: Credits are charged after the search completes based on results: 2 credits per company found and 2 credits per prospect found. Each query resolves to either companies or prospects, so only one rate applies per page.
x-credit-cost.comment: Your total charge depends on the number of results returned and which entity type the query resolves to.

domain.description: Company domain

linkedinUrl.description: LinkedIn company page URL using the numeric company ID (e.g. https://linkedin.com/company/1234). Null if unavailable.

industry.description: Primary industry. The value comes from the data provider and may vary in format.

countryCode.description: Company country (ISO alpha-3 code, e.g. USA)

linkedinUrl.description: LinkedIn profile URL

countryCode.description: Person's country (ISO alpha-3 code, e.g. USA)

companyLinkedinUrl.description: The person's current company LinkedIn URL

companyCountryCode.description: The person's current company headquarters country (ISO alpha-3 code, e.g. USA)

data.description: Search results — either companies or prospects, never both

nextCursor.description: Cursor for the next page. Pass this as `cursor` in a `{ request: "subsequent", cursor: "..." }` request. `null` means there are no more results. Cursors expire after 3 days.

post.description: Searches flight itineraries between cities of interest and returns trips, fares, timing, etc. ⚡ Rate limit: 120 requests per 1 minute 💰 Cost: 2 credits per search ⓘ

travelClass.description: Preferred cabin class. Omit to consider flights across all cabin classes.

infantsInSeat.description: Number of infants (under 2) with their own seat.

infantsOnLap.description: Number of infants (under 2) on an adult's lap.

maxStops.description: Maximum number of stops allowed. 0 = nonstop only, 1 = one stop or fewer, 2 = two stops or fewer. Omit to allow any number of stops.

sortBy.description: Sort criterion for results. 'top' ranks by overall value. 'price' sorts cheapest first. 'departureTime' and 'arrivalTime' sort earliest first. 'duration' sorts shortest first. 'emissions' sorts lowest carbon first. Direction is always ascending and cannot be changed. Omit to sort by 'top'.

include.description: Only return flights operated or marketed by these airlines. Pass 2-letter IATA airline codes (e.g. 'UA' for United, 'AA' for American, 'DL' for Delta, 'B6' for JetBlue). Case-insensitive.

exclude.description: Exclude flights operated or marketed by these airlines. Pass 2-letter IATA airline codes (e.g. 'UA' for United, 'AA' for American, 'DL' for Delta, 'B6' for JetBlue). Case-insensitive.

airlines.description: Filter by airline. By default all airlines are considered. If you pass 'include', only flights from those airlines are returned. If you pass 'exclude', flights from those airlines are removed.

minCarryOnBags.description: Minimum carry-on bags the itinerary must include. Omit for no requirement.

minCheckedBags.description: Minimum checked bags the itinerary must include. Omit for no requirement. Honored on a best-effort basis: not every itinerary exposes checked-bag inclusion.

maxPrice.description: Maximum total itinerary price in whole currency units. You may want to set `currencyCode` as well so the price cap is in the currency you expect (default currency is USD). Omit for no price cap.

startHour.description: Start of the hour range (inclusive), in 24-hour format.

endHour.description: End of the hour range (inclusive), in 24-hour format.

departure.description: Restrict departure times to this hour range.

arrival.description: Restrict arrival times to this hour range.

endHour.description: End of the hour range (inclusive), in 24-hour format.

returnTimeWindow.description: Time-of-day window for return flights (round-trip only). Both startHour and endHour must be provided together per sub-window.

minMinutes.description: Minimum layover duration in minutes. Omit for no minimum.

maxMinutes.description: Maximum layover duration in minutes. Omit for no maximum.

layoverDuration.description: Constrain layover duration. Omit to allow any layover length.

maxFlightDurationMinutes.description: Maximum total flight duration in minutes. Omit for no limit.

include.description: Only allow itineraries connecting through at least one of these IATA airports (e.g. 'DFW', 'SFO'). Nonstop flights and itineraries that don't match are filtered out. Narrow allowlists may return zero results. Case-insensitive.

exclude.description: Drop itineraries connecting through any of these IATA airports (e.g. 'ORD', 'ATL'). Case-insensitive.

connectingAirports.description: Filter by connecting airports. By default all connecting airports are allowed. We recommend not passing this unless you have a good reason — it significantly reduces the number of results returned.

onlyShowLowEmissionFlights.description: When true, only return flights with lower-than-typical carbon emissions. When false (default), return all flights.

showHidden.description: When true, include itineraries that would normally be hidden (e.g. very late or undesirable schedules).

hideSeparateTickets.description: When true, drop itineraries that combine separately-issued tickets (which carry higher disruption risk).

currencyCode.description: ISO 4217 currency code for prices in the response (e.g. 'EUR', 'GBP', 'CAD'). Case-insensitive. Defaults to USD.

searchMarketCountryCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code that sets the search market (e.g. 'GBR', 'BRA'). This affects regional pricing and flight availability — the same route may show different prices and options depending on the market. Case-insensitive.

languageCode.description: Language for search results (airport names, airline names, labels). Pass a BCP-47 language tag such as 'en', 'en-US', 'pt-BR', 'zh-CN', 'ja', 'ko', 'fr', 'de', 'es'.
